observations: Three photos show a dual-monitor setup on a desk, with a laptop in front.
Photo 0: Two monitors side by side, one displaying code with sticky notes, the other showing a mirrored setup with a webcam on top. The right monitor has a silver stand with a triangular base.
Photo 1: Same dual setup from a front angle, with a laptop closed in front, keyboard, and visible cables. The right monitor has a silver stand with a triangular base.
Photo 2: Darker shot, left monitor shows a dashboard with colorful tiles, right monitor shows code. The right monitor's stand is visible — silver, triangular base, matching photo 1.
No brand or model visible on any monitor bezel or stand in any photo.
The monitors appear to be 22-inch FHD, as claimed, based on size relative to keyboard and laptop.
The right monitor's stand is consistent with Dell or HP models, but no logo is visible.
No visible damage or dead pixels in the photos.
The seller claims IPS panel, 100% color accuracy, 60Hz — none of these specs are visible in the photos.

claims.evidence: Photos show monitors of plausible 22-inch size relative to keyboard and laptop, but no on-screen display or bezel text confirms size or resolution.
No visible panel type indicator. Cannot be confirmed from photos alone.
No calibration data or colorimeter results visible. Cannot be confirmed remotely.
No on-screen display or settings visible to confirm refresh rate.

risks.risk: Monitor may not be 22-inch FHD as claimed
risks.proof: Photo showing bezel with model number or on-screen display confirming size and resolution.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as smaller or lower resolution, which reduces value.

risks.risk: Panel type may not be IPS (could be TN or VA)
risks.proof: Photo showing monitor from side angles to check for color shift or viewing angle, or a close-up of the bezel with model number.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as TN panel, which is less valuable for professional use.

risks.risk: Color accuracy claim may be false or uncalibrated
risks.proof: Photo of monitor displaying a color calibration test pattern or a screenshot of calibration software.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as uncalibrated, reducing value for design or photo work.

risks.risk: Refresh rate may be lower than 60Hz (e.g., 50Hz or 48Hz)
risks.proof: Photo showing monitor settings menu with refresh rate displayed.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as lower refresh rate, reducing value for gaming or smooth scrolling.

risks.risk: One or both monitors may have dead pixels or physical damage
risks.proof: Photo showing monitor with full white or black screen to reveal dead pixels, or close-up of bezel for cracks or scratches.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as having potential dead pixels or damage, reducing value.

proof_requests: Photo of monitor bezel showing brand and model number.
Photo of monitor settings menu showing resolution, refresh rate, and panel type.
Photo of monitor displaying a full white screen to check for dead pixels.
Photo of monitor from side angle to check for color shift (IPS vs TN).
response.reason: The monitors cannot be identified by brand or model, and key claims (size, panel type, color accuracy, refresh rate) cannot be verified from the current photos. Without proof, the item cannot be priced accurately and risks being misvalued. The setup appears functional, but critical specs are unconfirmed.
